title: Face localization on monomial ideal tensors with unit coefficients
statement:
Let $P$ be an integral commutative monoid, written additively, meaning $P\to P^{\rm gp}$ is injective, and let $F\subset P$ be a face (a submonoid with $p+p'\in F$ implying $p,p'\in F$). Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$ a homomorphism sending $F$ to $A^\times$. Put $P_F=\{p-f:p\in P,f\in F\}\subset P^{\rm gp}$ and $\alpha_F(p-f)=\alpha(p)\alpha(f)^{-1}$. For a monoid ideal $H\subset P$, meaning $H+P\subset H$ and allowing $H=\varnothing$, put $H_F=\{h-f:h\in H,f\in F\}$. For any commutative ring $D$ and monoid $T$, write $D[T]$ for the finite sums $\sum d_tz^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$, and $D[K]\subset D[T]$ for the ideal with additive basis $z^k$, $k\in K$, when $K$ is a monoid ideal.
The extension of $\mathbf Z[H]$ to $\mathbf Z[P_F]$ is $\mathbf Z[H_F]$. Give $A$ the actions induced by $\alpha$ and $\alpha_F$. There is an $A$-linear isomorphism of module tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]
$$\lambda:\mathbf Z[H]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf Z[H_F]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P_F]}A,\qquad z^h\otimes a\longmapsto z^h\otimes a,$$
whose inverse is $z^{h-f}\otimes a\mapsto z^h\otimes\alpha(f)^{-1}a$, independent of the fraction representative. Both tensors have multiplication maps to $A$, respectively $z^h\otimes a\mapsto\alpha(h)a$ and $z^{h-f}\otimes a\mapsto\alpha_F(h-f)a$; $\lambda$ commutes with these maps and the identity on $A$. The isomorphism and its inverse commute with any coefficient homomorphism $\phi:A\to A'$ when the new chart is $\phi\alpha$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2 (printed p. 98) and proof of 3.4.3 (printed p. 110). Agent algebraic localization calculation on monomial ideal tensors; returned parent step 5 and monomial-basis clause of step 4.

proof.text: Regard $P$ as a submonoid of $P^{\rm gp}$ by integrality. Addition of representatives gives $(p-f)+(p'-f')=(p+p')-(f+f')$, so $P_F$ is a monoid containing $P$. If $p-f=p'-f'$, then $p+f'=p'+f$ in $P$; applying $\alpha$ and multiplying by the inverse of $\alpha(f)\alpha(f')$ proves $\alpha(p)\alpha(f)^{-1}=\alpha(p')\alpha(f')^{-1}$. Thus $\alpha_F$ is well defined, multiplicative, and extends $\alpha$. Moreover $(h-f)+(p-g)=(h+p)-(f+g)\in H_F$, so $H_F$ is a monoid ideal. None of these assertions requires finite generation, saturation, or a nonempty $H$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideals); agent calculation, step 1.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z[P]$, $S=\mathbf Z[P_F]$, $I=\mathbf Z[H]$, $J=\mathbf Z[H_F]$ and $M=I\otimes_R A$, $N=J\otimes_S A$. All products of a monomial in the image of $I$ with a monomial of $S$ have exponent $h+(p-f)=(h+p)-f\in H_F$; hence the extended ideal $IS$ is contained in $J$. Conversely each additive basis vector $z^{h-f}$ of $J$ is $z^h z^{-f}$ and belongs to $IS$. Taking finite integer linear combinations proves $IS=J$, including $H=\varnothing$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideals); agent calculation, step 2.

proof.text: For $i\in I$ and $a\in A$, send $(i,a)$ to $i\otimes_S a\in N$, using the inclusion $I\to J$. This is additive in both entries and $R$-bilinear, since $(ri)\otimes_S a=i\otimes_S\alpha(r)a$ for $r\in R$ (here $\alpha$ denotes the induced ring map). The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $\lambda:M\to N$. It is $A$-linear: on pure tensors $\lambda(i\otimes ca)=i\otimes ca=c\lambda(i\otimes a)$, and pure tensors generate. In particular $\lambda(z^h\otimes a)=z^h\otimes a$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideal tensors); agent calculation, step 3. Tensor universal property: Stacks Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, algebra.tex.

proof.text:
Define on a monomial of $J$ the prospective inverse value $\beta(z^{h-f},a)=z^h\otimes_R\alpha(f)^{-1}a\in M$. To check representatives, suppose $h-f=h'-f'$, so integrality gives $h+f'=h'+f$ in $P$. For $b=\alpha(f)^{-1}\alpha(f')^{-1}a$, tensor balancing [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives
$$z^h\otimes\alpha(f)^{-1}a=z^{h+f'}\otimes b=z^{h'+f}\otimes b=z^{h'}\otimes\alpha(f')^{-1}a.$$
The exponents $h+f'$ and $h'+f$ belong to $H$ by its ideal property. This proves representative independence without cancellation of any nonunit scalar in $A$. Extend $\beta$ by finite integer linear combinations in $J$; the monomial basis makes the extension unique. It is additive in both arguments and $A$-linear in the second.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideal tensors); agent calculation, step 4. Tensor universal property: Stacks Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, algebra.tex.

proof.text:
It remains to check $S$-balancing. For $h\in H$, $f,g\in F$, $p\in P$, the formula and $R$-balancing give
$$\begin{aligned}\beta(z^{h-f}z^{p-g},a)&=z^{h+p}\otimes\alpha(f+g)^{-1}a\\&=z^h\otimes\alpha(p)\alpha(f)^{-1}\alpha(g)^{-1}a\\&=\beta(z^{h-f},\alpha_F(p-g)a).\end{aligned}$$
Here $h+p\in H$ and $f+g\in F$. Expanding finite sums proves the relation for every element of $S$ and every element of $J$. Give $M$ its $S$-action through $\alpha_F:S\to A$; then the displayed relation and $A$-linearity in the second argument say exactly that $\beta:J\times A\to M$ is $S$-bilinear. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $\mu:N\to M$, $z^{h-f}\otimes a\mapsto z^h\otimes\alpha(f)^{-1}a$, and the same formula shows that $\mu$ is $A$-linear.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideal tensors); agent calculation, step 5. Tensor universal property: Stacks Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, algebra.tex.

proof.text:
For $h\in H$, using $f=0$ gives $\mu\lambda(z^h\otimes a)=z^h\otimes a$. Conversely $S$-balancing and $z^h=z^{h-f}z^f$ give
$$\lambda\mu(z^{h-f}\otimes a)=z^h\otimes\alpha(f)^{-1}a=z^{h-f}\otimes\alpha(f)\alpha(f)^{-1}a=z^{h-f}\otimes a.$$
The monomials additively generate $I$ and $J$, and pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so these identities prove $\mu\lambda=1_M$ and $\lambda\mu=1_N$. Thus $\lambda$ is the stated $A$-linear isomorphism with the specified inverse.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideal tensors); agent calculation, step 6. Tensor universal property: Stacks Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, algebra.tex.

proof.text: Evaluation of a finite sum at $\alpha$ or $\alpha_F$ is additive and respects multiplication. Consequently the pairings $(i,a)\mapsto\alpha(i)a$ and $(j,a)\mapsto\alpha_F(j)a$ are respectively $R$- and $S$-bilinear and give the multiplication maps by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On $z^h\otimes a$, the two composites to $A$ both equal $\alpha(h)a$. For the inverse formula the value is $\alpha(h)\alpha(f)^{-1}a=\alpha_F(h-f)a$. Additivity and generation by monomial pure tensors prove the asserted commuting square.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (monoid localization), and proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial ideal tensors); agent calculation, step 7. Tensor universal property: Stacks Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, algebra.tex.

proof.text: Let $\phi:A\to A'$ be a coefficient homomorphism and $\alpha'=\phi\alpha$. The coefficient maps $M\to M'$ and $N\to N'$ send $z^h\otimes a\mapsto z^h\otimes\phi(a)$ and $z^{h-f}\otimes a\mapsto z^{h-f}\otimes\phi(a)$; the balancing relations are respected because $\phi(\alpha(p)a)=\alpha'(p)\phi(a)$ and likewise for $\alpha_F$. Thus these maps descend from the tensor presentations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. They commute with $\lambda$ on every monomial pure tensor. They commute with $\mu$ because $\phi(\alpha(f)^{-1}a)=\alpha'(f)^{-1}\phi(a)$: a ring homomorphism sends a unit and its inverse to inverse units. Expanding sums gives both naturality squares.
